clue.text: Does this building on site need a skeleton staff ?

definitions.text: Does this building on site need a skeleton staff ?

parts.words: Does this building on site need a skeleton staff
parts.note: a skeleton staff is a minimal workforce, but here the skeleton is the timber structure the building is put up around

explanation.surface: A question about whether a construction project can run with only a handful of workers.
explanation.definitionFit: A frame house is built on a timber skeleton, which is then clad.

clue.text: Send another message to improve current relations

definitions.meaning: wire once meant send a telegram
renew the electric wiring that carries current

explanation.surface: Diplomats send a fresh dispatch to mend relations.
explanation.definitionFit: To rewire is to telegraph again or to replace electrical circuits.

clue.text: Orange sort of duck?

definitions.meaning: a small citrus fruit like a tangerine

explanation.surface: Someone wonders about duck à l'orange.
explanation.definitionFit: A mandarin is a small citrus fruit, and the mandarin duck is an ornamental waterfowl.

clue.text: Hope to include Thomas Stearns? Right bloomer that is!

indicators.note: one word holds the others inside it

parts.note: the poet T. S. Eliot

explanation.surface: Hope taking in a famous poet seems a correct mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' looks like a blunder but means a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Heliotrope is a garden plant with fragrant purple flowers.

clue.text: A French strait that is not reliable:

parts.note: un is French for a
a sound is a narrow sea channel

explanation.surface: A sea channel in France proves treacherous.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsound means faulty or untrustworthy.

clue.text: Girl told' to eat up ?

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: to dine is to eat

explanation.surface: A girl is told to finish her meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Enid is a female name.

clue.text: 'It's frightful, but could be made more safe

indicators.note: the answer could be formed from these letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Something scary might be made safer.
explanation.definitionFit: Fearsome means terrifying, inspiring dread.

clue.text: Flower girls we hear this way

indicators.note: what we hear is what the names sound like when spoken

parts.note: Polly and Ann are two girls' names
thus means in this manner

explanation.surface: Some girls are overheard going in a certain direction.
explanation.definitionFit: A polyanthus is a hybrid primula grown as a garden plant.

clue.text: All stay in metaphysics ?. Not I !

definitions.meaning: in metaphysics, the ... is everything outside the conscious self

explanation.surface: A philosopher insists nobody leaves while disowning a claim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in metaphysics' tells you the second sense is a technical term of philosophy.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase 'none go' means everyone stays, while the philosophical term means the external world, what is not the self.

clue.text: Pickwickian enters the back way, gives star performance

indicators.note: one piece going into another is put inside it
taking the street the back way means reading its abbreviation backwards

parts.note: ST is short for street, a way
Mr Winkle is one of the club members in Dickens's The Pickwick Papers

explanation.surface: A Dickens character slips in through the rear entrance and puts on a stellar show.
explanation.definitionFit: A star twinkles, so to twinkle is to perform as a star does.

clue.text: Mr Hawk senior's the very devil!

parts.note: senior means old, the elder
a harrier is a kind of hawk, so the hawk is jokily given the man's name Harry

explanation.surface: An elderly gentleman called Hawk turns out to be a thoroughly wicked character.
explanation.walkthrough: The hawk here is the harrier, so its 'Mr' becomes HARRY.
explanation.definitionFit: Old Harry is an old nickname for Satan.

clue.text: Look at the fellow !

definitions.meaning: to look closely or squint at something
an equal, a person of the same rank

explanation.surface: Someone points out a man in the street.
explanation.definitionFit: To peer is to gaze closely, and a peer is one's equal or companion.

clue.text: A disparaging word for poor Private Joe

indicators.note: a poor version is a mangled one, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A slur aimed at an unfortunate soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: A pejorative is a term expressing contempt.

clue.text: Shady.U.S. district joint

definitions.meaning: a seedy, vice-ridden quarter of an American city, originally in New York
a joint of meat, the tenderest cut of beef or pork

explanation.surface: A dodgy American neighbourhood bar.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tenderloin was New York's notorious vice quarter, and tenderloin is also the fillet cut of meat.

clue.text: Raise sort of Blue Peter a new way to vex us

indicators.note: in a down entry, raising a word reads it from bottom up

parts.note: saxe is a light greyish-blue

indicators.note: putting letters a new way rearranges them

explanation.surface: Hoisting a flag in an unfamiliar fashion annoys the crew.
explanation.walkthrough: A Blue Peter is a signal flag, but 'Blue' goes with 'sort of' (SAXE, raised to EXAS) and PETER is the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To exasperate is to irritate intensely.

clue.text: Preacher-poet loses two points to man in an old suit

indicators.note: losing something means it is taken away from the name

parts.note: John Donne was a metaphysical poet and Dean of St Paul's
N is north, a compass point, taken twice

explanation.surface: A clergyman-poet gets two marks docked, leaving a figure from an antiquated lawsuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suit' is a lawsuit: the fictitious name was used in old English ejectment actions.
explanation.definitionFit: The placeholder name was used for a fictitious party in legal actions.

clue.text: Innkeeper could involve 4 with loss of work

indicators.note: the letters could be worked round to form the answer
a piece is dropped from the cross-referenced answer before the rest is rearranged

parts.note: the answer to 4 down
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A landlord might take on a flower but lose some work.
explanation.walkthrough: 4 is HELIOTROPE; 'with loss of' removes OP, and 'could involve' rearranges what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotelier runs a hotel or inn.

clue.text: Castle very hard outside — clear inside needs repair

indicators.note: the pencil grade wraps around the other piece
the scrambled word sits within the pencil grade

parts.note: HH is the pencil grade for very hard lead

indicators.note: something needing repair must be put back together, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A fortress with tough outer walls whose interior is falling apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needs repair' rearranges CLEAR to ARLEC, which 'outside'/'inside' place between the two H's.
explanation.definitionFit: Harlech Castle is a medieval fortress in north Wales.

clue.text: An outside chance this came from Tom's gun ?

definitions.meaning: a bet with little chance of winning
a Long Tom is a long-barrelled cannon, so its discharge is its shot

explanation.surface: Someone's slim hope was a shot fired by Tom.
explanation.definitionFit: A long shot is an unlikely venture, and also a shot from a long gun.

clue.text: Chapter One follows Greek account of the. Roman brothers

indicators.note: one piece coming after another is placed later

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: The first chapter of a Greek history covers two Roman brothers.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gracchi, Tiberius and Gaius, were Roman tribunes who pushed land reform.

clue.text: Old crock of a sort of snake catcher

parts.note: the rattle names the rattlesnake
a trap catches animals

explanation.surface: A ramshackle device for catching snakes.
explanation.definitionFit: A rattletrap is a decrepit, noisy old vehicle.

clue.text: Where sporting practice brings an automatic return

indicators.note: a return goes back, so the gun's name is read backwards

parts.note: the Sten is a British submachine gun

explanation.surface: A training ground where shots come straight back.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, batsmen practise in netted lanes; the automatic is a gun, not a ball machine.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricketers practise batting and bowling in enclosures of netting.

clue.text: As ink-maker the girl is in the money

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: tin is old slang for money
Ann is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl strikes it rich as a maker of ink.
explanation.definitionFit: Tannin was combined with iron salts to make traditional writing ink.

clue.text: Strange rite — cull produce of the earth

indicators.note: something strange is out of order, so the letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: An odd ritual of culling yields something from the soil.
explanation.definitionFit: Telluric means terrestrial, from Latin tellus, ground.

clue.text: Last thing to bring up !

explanation.surface: A final reminder of a topic to raise.
explanation.definitionFit: The rear is the hindmost part, and to rear is to raise young.

clue.text: Many whips active for the Opposition?

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, many
whips in action are lashing

explanation.surface: Lots of party whips busy on behalf of the parliamentary Opposition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'whips' suggests parliamentary whips but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Clashing things are in conflict, set against each other.

clue.text: This steak is capital

definitions.meaning: a dish of minced beef patty named after a city
the seat of government of Austria

explanation.surface: Someone praises a steak as excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: Vienna steak is a fried minced beef patty, and the city is Austria's capital.

clue.text: For the seer nothing detailed can come of this crystal

indicators.note: the answer may be made out of these letters, rearranged
with its tail removed, the word loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A crystal ball that shows nothing to a clairvoyant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' cuts NOTHING to NOTHIN; 'can come of' rearranges SEER plus NOTHIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhinestone is an imitation diamond made of rock crystal or glass.
